findings.problem:
This diff is a byte-for-byte revert of commit d47b4c2 (`fix(security): prevent potential key leakage in validate_connection log messages`), which deliberately replaced `exc=exc` with sanitized fields (`status=exc.response.status_code`, `count=exc.error_count()`) specifically to stop raw httpx/pydantic exception text from reaching logs. That fix was added even though triggarr/logging.py already had its custom redacting sink (present since the Feb 2026 commit, well before the Apr 2026 fix) -- i.e. the maintainer judged the sink alone insufficient and added this call-site sanitization as a second layer. This diff removes that second layer with no replacement and no explanation.

The redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py:36-41) only does exact string-replacement of a short list of currently-configured secret VALUES (arr api keys, session secret, password hash -- see triggarr/startup.py:90-96, triggarr/web/routes.py). It is not a general sensitive-data filter. The pydantic.ValidationError branch (triggarr/clients/base.py:250-256) now logs `str(exc)`, and SystemStatus (triggarr/models/arr.py:54-63) requires only `version: str` with `extra="ignore"`. For a pydantic v2 'missing field' error, the ValidationError's default string representation embeds the full `input_value`, which for a top-level required-field-missing error is the ENTIRE response dict passed to `model_validate()` -- i.e. the complete raw JSON body returned by the user's Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr instance (paths, OS info, instance name, auth mode, etc.), none of which matches the sink's known-secrets list and so passes through unredacted. That log line also feeds the in-app log buffer rendered to the web UI log viewer (triggarr/web/routes.py:1195, log_buffer.get_recent), a surface this same project's own backlog (999.3) already flags as having previously leaked sensitive data (reset tokens) to viewers.

For the httpx.HTTPStatusError branch (base.py:225-237), the specific call site (`self._client.get(self._status_path)`, no query params) does not currently put the X-Api-Key header value into the URL, so str(exc) for this exact call wouldn't carry the configured API key today -- the demonstrated exposure here is weaker and mostly reinstates the risk the original fix was written to close rather than a confirmed secret leak under the current code paths.
findings.title: Revert of named security fix reintroduces raw exception logging (CWE-532)
findings.why_it_matters: This reopens a vulnerability the project already identified and fixed by name ('prevent potential key leakage'). The existing redacting sink is a narrow, exact-match secret scrubber, not a general log-sanitization layer, so full exception text -- including embedded raw API response bodies on validation failures -- now flows to stderr and the web log viewer unredacted.

agent_notes: The diff takes the shape of an intentional revert of the sanitized logging. There is no intent document or commit message saying the more verbose diagnostics are wanted. If they are, the consistent approach is to change `_sanitize_exc` and the two inline copies together, not just validate_connection.

Duplication note, not a finding: the inline `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}" if isinstance(exc, httpx.HTTPStatusError) else type(exc).__name__` expression appears in triggarr/clients/base.py:71-75 and triggarr/tracking.py:70-74, and `_sanitize_exc` in triggarr/search/engine.py is a superset of it. That makes three implementations of the same idea, all private to their modules. Moving `_sanitize_exc` into a shared module (e.g. triggarr/clients/base.py or triggarr/logging.py) would make it easy for clients, tracking and engine to stay consistent, and would have made this regression stand out.

`_sanitize_exc`'s docstring says raw str(exc) may 'bypass the loguru redacting sink'. triggarr/logging.py redacts the full formatted output, so configured secrets are still scrubbed. The remaining risk is non-secret but sensitive content (URLs, internal hosts, response bodies). The API key is sent in the X-Api-Key header, not the URL, so str(HTTPStatusError) should not contain it directly.

No tests assert on the 'Unexpected HTTP error' or 'Unexpected API response format' messages (grep of tests/), so this change is untested in both directions. Neither the old nor the new log format is pinned.

No new imports, dependencies, cycles or cross-module coupling. The change is confined to log-message formatting in ArrClient.validate_connection, and the subclasses (lidarr/radarr/sonarr) inherit it unchanged.

findings.problem: The old code logged only `exc.response.status_code`. The diff now logs the whole exception object. In the installed httpx, the HTTPStatusError message is built at .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_models.py:816 as "... for url '{0.url}'". `httpx.URL.__str__` (_urls.py:374) returns the raw URI with userinfo left unmasked. Only `__repr__` masks it. The client keeps userinfo on request.url, because _client.py:469 reads request.url.username/password to build BasicAuth. Config validation still accepts both leaking shapes. validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:112-157) checks only the scheme, the hostname and blocked IPs, so userinfo passes. reject_apikey_in_url (triggarr/models/config.py:65-89) rejects only keys that start with `apikey`, and its docstring says `?token=foo` stays valid for reverse-proxy setups. Concrete trigger: an instance url of `https://bob:s3cret@arr.example/` or `https://proxy/sonarr?token=abc` where /api/v3/system/status returns any non-401 error (403 from the proxy, 404 for a wrong subpath, 500 or 502). The call path is startup.py:160 -> validate_connection -> the else branch at base.py:232. The log line then contains `s3cret` or `token=abc`. The redacting sinks (triggarr/logging.py:36-42 and 72-82) replace only values collected by startup.collect_secrets, meaning *arr API keys and auth secrets, so URL passwords and proxy tokens go unredacted to stderr and to log_buffer, which feeds the web UI log viewer. A 3xx response also adds the Location header to the message (_models.py:810-811), so an SSO redirect URL ends up in the log too. The repo already has a helper that guards this exact property, `_sanitize_exc` (triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44), and the scheduler uses it for this reason (scheduler.py:218-234, 400-410). The same file uses the same sanitization in `_request_with_retry` (base.py:71-75). This diff removes that guarantee from the changed line.

Both findings are soft/style-adjacent pattern-consistency observations, not security or correctness defects; surfaced per coverage instructions despite low confidence.

agent_notes: Do not ship: expanded exception logging exposes configured proxy tokens.

findings.fix_hint: Keep logging the status code instead of the raw exception, or explicitly strip credentials and query values before logging. Add a regression test using a configured URL token and a 502 response against both logging sinks.
findings.problem: A supported URL such as https://proxy.example/arr?token=proxy-secret passes InstanceConfig validation and reaches validate_connection through startup.py:154–160. On a 502 response, the newly logged HTTPStatusError includes the request URL and proxy-secret (verified with installed HTTPX). collect_secrets only collects API keys and auth secrets, so neither logging sink redacts this URL token. Previously this branch logged only the status code; now the credential reaches stderr and the web log buffer.
